name: EY-Parthenon
seo_title: EY-Parthenon case interview and Experience Day guide
description: What EY's own careers pages say about joining EY-Parthenon: online assessments, the Experience Day, interviews and case studies, with sources.
intro: This guide sums up what EY-Parthenon's own careers pages say about applying and interviewing, from how to apply to how EY-Parthenon suggests you prepare. It reflects those pages as we checked them on 16 October 2026. Processes differ by programme, role and country, so check EY-Parthenon's careers site for your role before you apply.

items.text: For its UK early careers programmes, EY says you create an account, choose a programme and location, and can apply for only one programme every six months.
EY says UK early careers applications do not need a CV or cover letter, and every applicant fills in the same online application form.

For its UK early careers programmes, EY says the assessment process includes a Realistic Job Preview, a first stage of online assessment covering teamwork and learning capability, and also a behavioural skills test.

EY says its UK early careers online assessments may ask you to pick from several options, read a table, chart or graph, move or drag items on screen, spot a pattern or apply rules, or record a video response.
EY says the online assessment has a time limit, and you see instructions and example questions before the timed part begins.
EY's UK early careers assessment rules say you must complete every assessment yourself without any help, and must not share any assessment material with anyone else.
For its UK graduate programmes, EY says candidates who pass the online assessment stages are invited to an EY Experience Day.
EY says Experience Days for its UK graduate, industrial placement and apprentice programmes are held in its UK offices, while for all summer internships the Experience Day is virtual.
For its UK graduate programmes, EY says that if your programme includes a final interview, it usually takes place two to three weeks after the EY Experience Day, subject to a successful outcome.
For experienced hires in the UK, EY says it interviews virtually or in person and may also ask for a presentation, case study or technical assessment, depending on the service line and role.

For UK experienced hires, EY says that, depending on the role, you may be asked case study or scenario-based questions, which test your analytical thinking, commercial awareness and how you approach real business problems.
EY-Parthenon's US careers page says hiring processes, needs and timelines vary by country and are run by each country.

For its US Associate Program, EY-Parthenon says candidates can expect a mix of behavioural and case-based interviews with several EY-Parthenon professionals, and offer decisions usually come within a week.

For students and entry-level candidates in the Netherlands, EY-Parthenon says the first round at its office is a numerical test, an interview with a recruiter and two case interviews, and the final round is three interviews with an Associate Partner or Partner.

For its Australian graduate programme, EY-Parthenon Strategy says interviews usually run over two or three rounds, and the first round includes two 'blind' problem-solving interviews, where the interviewer knows nothing about you until you meet.
EY-Parthenon Strategy in Australia says its problem-solving interviews are based on a real-world business scenario or case study and assess how you think rather than what you know.

EY-Parthenon Strategy in Australia says the problem-solving interviews are followed, usually on the same day, by a more traditional interview about your experience, interests, motivation for consulting and understanding of the firm.

For its UK early careers programmes, EY lists eight key skills: being proactive, doing the right thing, being curious, building relationships, showing agility, thinking critically, embracing technology and being motivated.

For its UK EY-Parthenon Strategy (Public and Private) graduate programme and summer internship, EY lists five core skills: problem solving, analytical thinking, confidence in ambiguity, inclusive collaboration and digital fluency.
For its UK early careers programmes, EY says it offers a preparation hub inside the assessment portal where you can practise the assessments as you move through the stages.
For experienced hires in the UK, EY advises studying the job description, researching EY and why you want to join, and preparing examples using the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result).

EY-Parthenon Strategy in Australia advises candidates not to lean on a memorised script or a framework researched in advance, and instead to engage with the case and structure and explain their thinking clearly.

EY-Parthenon Strategy in Australia says the best candidates talk interviewers through their structure and thinking as they work, and advises listening and asking questions rather than rushing to a solution.

practice_advice: Practise saying your structure out loud before you start any analysis, so the interviewer can follow your plan.
Do short, timed mental maths drills most days, with pen and paper only. Mock Partner's drills cover mental maths, chart reading and market sizing.
After each practice case, write down one thing to do better and choose your next case to work on it.
